chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sukuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon them both, from the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family, who said:
Women are four: Jami' Mujma', Rabi' Murabba', Kurb Muqma', and Ghull Qaml.

key_terms.جَامِعٌ مُجْمَعٌ: Comprehensive and agreed upon (a type of woman)
key_terms.رَبِيعٌ مُرَبَّعٌ: Spring-like and square/complete (a type of woman)
key_terms.غُلٌّ قَمَلٌ: Louse-like or numerous/small (a type of woman)
key_terms.كَرْبٌ مُقْمَعٌ: Close and pressed/compact (a type of woman)

ai.seo_question: What are the four types of women described in the hadith from Maani al-Akhbar?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* presents a concise typology of women using four compound descriptors, reflecting the classical Arabic rhetorical style of pairing synonyms for emphasis. While the exact semantic nuances of terms like 'Ghull Qaml' (often interpreted as numerous or small) are subject to scholarly interpretation, the classification serves to categorize women based on their social presence, physical or spiritual completeness, and distinct characteristics. It highlights the Shia tradition’s appreciation for nuanced linguistic analysis in understanding human archetypes as narrated through the Imams.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, from Abdullah bin Muhammed bin Isa, from his father, from Abdullah bin Mughaira, from Isma’eel bin Abi Ziyad al-Sukuni, from Ja’far bin Muhammed, from his father, peace be upon them both, from the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, that he said:
Women are four: jami’ mujma’, rabee’ murabba’, kurb muqma’ and ghull qaml.
